new_packages.label_en: Speech and the Revelation of the Soul
new_packages.reason: The Torah's single conceptual cluster connects speech (דיבור), soul-revelation (התגלות הנפש והלב), and the scriptural verse 'נַפְשִׁי יָצְאָה בְדַבְּרוֹ' through an explicit bechina identity: 'הַדִּבּוּר בְּעַצְמוֹ הוּא הִתְגַּלּוּת הַנֶּפֶשׁ וְהַלֵּב'. All three are expressions of the same essential reality — speech and soul-going-out are not cause and effect; they are the same event viewed from two angles. The verse-node anchors the identification in Scripture. These concepts form an independent domain: the metaphysics of authentic speech as an inherently soulful act.

edges.proof: זֶהוּ בְּעַצְמוֹ שֶׁמְּדַבֵּר הוּא בְּחִינַת הִתְגַּלּוּת הִתְעוֹרְרוּת לִבּוֹ וְנַפְשׁוֹ לְהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ... שֶׁהַדִּבּוּר בְּעַצְמוֹ הוּא הִתְגַּלּוּת הַנֶּפֶשׁ וְהַלֵּב
בִּבְחִינַת (שיר השירים ה׳:ו׳): נַפְשִׁי יָצְאָה בְדַבְּרוֹ — the verse is cited as the scriptural bechina-ground for the equation between speech and soul-revelation

new_packages.mirror_notes: This Torah presents no evil counterpart. The teaching is entirely positive: speech as the medium and expression of holiness. The opposing force — the state where one 'has no heart' (אֵין לוֹ לֵב) — is mentioned incidentally as the condition one is overcoming, not as an elaborated evil package with its own bechina structure.

observations:
Torah LM2/98 is a short, concentrated teaching on hitbodedut and personal prayer. Despite its brevity, it contains a clear and structurally independent bechina cluster.

The central thesis: speech (דיבור) in the context of supplication IS — not merely produces — the revelation of the soul and heart to God. The Rebbe states this identity twice: first calling the act of speaking 'בְּחִינַת הִתְגַּלּוּת הִתְעוֹרְרוּת לִבּוֹ וְנַפְשׁוֹ' and then, at the close, summarizing 'הַדִּבּוּר בְּעַצְמוֹ הוּא הִתְגַּלּוּת הַנֶּפֶשׁ וְהַלֵּב'. The repetition and the word 'בְּעַצְמוֹ' (itself/by itself) confirm this is bechina: the Rebbe is saying speech and soul-revelation are the same thing, not that one produces the other.

The verse 'נַפְשִׁי יָצְאָה בְדַבְּרוֹ' (Song of Songs 5:6) is cited as the scriptural ground for this equation. The soul going out IS the speaking — they are simultaneous and identical.

The eitza dimension (that sustained speech eventually produces great arousal even when one starts without heart) appears in the third sentence and is structurally distinct from the bechina teaching. The bechina: speech = soul-revelation. The eitza: sustained speech → arousal arrives.

This package — דִּבּוּר וְהִתְגַּלּוּת הַנֶּפֶשׁ — qualifies as a new package proposal because:
1. It contains 3 nodes connected by explicit bechina language from the source text.
2. It represents an independent conceptual domain: the ontology of authentic speech as inherently soulful.
3. It is entirely absent from the dataset (reference=1098 has zero entries of any type).

The package has no evil mirror in this Torah. The 'lack of heart' is mentioned as a subjective feeling the person may have, not as an elaborated evil counterforce with its own bechina structure. The teaching is purely positive in its orientation.
